- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.7) and understate when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.3).  
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day trend.  
- After sharp price spikes, model overcorrects downward; reduce forecast overshoot by 5–15% in subsequent periods.  
- Mean reversion is strong in low-sentiment periods; model fails to reflect this, so dampen forecasts when sentiment is flat or negative.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values.
